theme: 3 terms on what is inside an app: the unique name that tells apps apart, the folder that holds the running app's files, and the key-value file format Apple uses for settings

terms.definition: A unique name for your app, usually written in reverse domain style, that iOS and the App Store use to tell apps apart.
terms.example: The staging app has its own Bundle Identifier, so both apps fit on one phone.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let id = Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier
print(id ?? "none")

terms.definition: The folder that holds your running app's code and resources, reached in code with `Bundle.main`.
terms.example: The image isn't in the Main Bundle, check its target membership.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let url = Bundle.main.url(
    forResource: "Colors",
    withExtension: "json")
print(url == nil ? "missing" : "found")

terms.definition: A file format Apple uses to store settings as keys and values, in XML or binary.
terms.example: Put the feature flags in a Property List, so we can change them without touching code.
terms.code:
import Foundation
let key = "CFBundleShortVersionString"
let v = Bundle.main
    .object(forInfoDictionaryKey: key)
print(v ?? "none")

video.description:
Learn to explain what is inside an iOS app: Bundle Identifier, Main Bundle & Property List, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Bundle Identifier - A unique name for your app, usually written in reverse domain style, that iOS and the App Store use to tell apps apart.
Main Bundle - The folder that holds your running app's code and resources, reached in code with `Bundle.main`.
Property List - A file format Apple uses to store settings as keys and values, in XML or binary.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Bundle Identifier, Main Bundle & Property List in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
번들 식별자, 메인 번들, 프로퍼티 리스트 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Bundle Identifier - A unique name for your app, usually written in reverse domain style, that iOS and the App Store use to tell apps apart.
한국어: 번들 식별자: 보통 도메인을 거꾸로 쓴 형태로, iOS와 App Store가 앱을 서로 구분하는 데 쓰는 고유한 이름

Main Bundle - The folder that holds your running app's code and resources, reached in code with `Bundle.main`.
한국어: 메인 번들: 실행 중인 앱의 코드와 리소스가 들어 있는 폴더로, 코드에서는 `Bundle.main`으로 접근함

Property List - A file format Apple uses to store settings as keys and values, in XML or binary.
한국어: 프로퍼티 리스트: Apple이 설정을 키와 값으로 저장할 때 쓰는 XML 또는 바이너리 파일 형식

landscape.hook: The app crashes loading one file. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Where did Config go?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the app crashes on launch, right at `url`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: `Config`, our Property List with the server address.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then the Main Bundle can't find it. Is it in the target?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oh, target membership was off. So it never got copied.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Only files in the target end up in the Main Bundle.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can the staging build use a different file?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sure. Staging has its own Bundle Identifier, so the code can check it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Isn't the Bundle Identifier also stored in a Property List?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, in the Info plist. That's a Property List too, just keys and values.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. With the file in the Main Bundle, `url` won't be nil.
Staging gets its own Bundle Identifier, so both apps fit on one phone.
